title: Build a Matrix With Conditions
summary: Build a k×k matrix containing each value from 1 through k exactly once, with zeros in all other cells.

contractDetails.constraints: 2 ≤ k ≤ 400. Each rule list contains 1–10000 pairs of distinct labels in [1,k]. Repeated rules are allowed. A valid result has exactly k rows and k columns.
contractDetails.output-checking: Accept any k×k matrix with each label exactly once, valid row and column prerequisites, and zeros elsewhere. Accept an empty matrix only when a prerequisite graph has a cycle.

statement: Build a k×k matrix containing each value from 1 through k exactly once, with zeros in all other cells. Each row rule [a,b] places a strictly above b. Each column rule places a strictly left of b. Return any matrix satisfying every rule, or an empty matrix when impossible.

examples.explanation: This diagonal placement meets both rules.
The row rules require both labels to be above one another.
2 is higher, while 1 is farther left.

constraints: 2 ≤ k ≤ 400. Each rule list contains 1–10000 pairs of distinct labels in [1,k]. Repeated rules are allowed. A valid result has exactly k rows and k columns.
hints: Conceptual: Row and column rules can be solved separately.
Directional: Treat each rule set as its own directed graph.
Implementation: Topologically order both graphs, then place each label at the intersection of its row position and column position. A cycle in either graph prevents a solution.
complexityAnalysis: O(k²+R+C) time and O(k²) space for adjacency matrices and output, where R and C are rule counts.
